# Disagreement Log — Didache Chapter 4

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Chapter:** Didache 4 — Further Ethics; Close of the Two Ways
**Agents:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA

---

## Summary
Total disagreements: 7

---

## Disagreement 1 — v.1: τὸ κυριακὸν τῆς κυριότητος — rendering the presence-theology phrase

| Agent | Rendering |
|-------|-----------|
| EMET | "wherever the lordly nature is spoken of, there the Lord is" |
| LOGOS | "where the Lord's authority is proclaimed, there the Lord himself is present" |
| PNEUMA | "wherever the Lord's authority is spoken, the Lord is there" |

**Issue:** This is the most difficult phrase in ch. 4. It asserts a kind of real presence of the Lord wherever the word of the Lord is proclaimed. EMET's "lordly nature" is too abstract; LOGOS's rendering is the most theologically precise.
**Ruling:** LOGOS adopted with minor adjustment.

---

## Disagreement 2 — v.2: "faces of the saints" vs. "company of the saints"

| Agent | Rendering |
|-------|-----------|
| EMET | "seek out daily the faces of the saints" |
| LOGOS | "seek out daily the company of the saints" |
| PNEUMA | "make a point of being with God's people every day" |

**Issue:** The Greek "faces" (πρόσωπα) is a Semitism for "presence/company of." EMET's literalness produces an unusual phrase. LOGOS clarifies without over-paraphrasing.
**Ruling:** "The company of the saints" (LOGOS) adopted.

---

## Disagreement 3 — v.6: "means of your hands" vs. "what you earn by your labor"

| Agent | Rendering |
|-------|-----------|
| EMET | "if you have the means of your hands" |
| LOGOS | "if you have earned anything by your labor" |
| PNEUMA | "whatever you earn with your hands" |

**Issue:** ἐργασία τῶν χειρῶν σου = the work/earnings of your hands. EMET is stilted; LOGOS and PNEUMA are clearer.
**Ruling:** "Whatever you have earned by your labor" adopted (blend of LOGOS and PNEUMA).

---

## Disagreement 4 — v.8: ἀθάνατα/θνητά — "immortal/mortal" vs. "imperishable/perishable"

| Agent | Rendering |
|-------|-----------|
| EMET | "immortal things / mortal things" |
| LOGOS | "imperishable / perishable" |
| PNEUMA | "eternal life / earthly goods" |

**Issue:** PNEUMA interprets too freely. EMET and LOGOS differ on a legitimate translation choice.
**Ruling:** "Imperishable/perishable" (LOGOS) adopted for the contrast in the a fortiori argument.

---

## Disagreement 5 — v.10: δοῦλος/δούλη — "slave" vs. "servant"

| Agent | Rendering |
|-------|-----------|
| EMET | "male slave / female slave" |
| LOGOS | "male or female servant" |
| PNEUMA | "slaves" |

**Issue:** δοῦλος = slave (chattel slavery in Greco-Roman context). LOGOS's "servant" softens the term. EMET's "male slave / female slave" is accurate but awkward. PNEUMA's simple "slaves" is clear.
**Ruling:** "Male or female servant" retained as a compromise. A translator note clarifies that δοῦλος refers to enslaved persons in the ancient context.

---

## Disagreement 6 — v.10: "reputation" vs. "partiality" — God's impartiality

| Agent | Rendering |
|-------|-----------|
| EMET | "not to call according to reputation" |
| LOGOS | "not call people based on status" |
| PNEUMA | "doesn't play favorites" |

**Issue:** The Greek κατὰ πρόσωπον (according to face/appearance) is an idiom for partiality/status (prosōpolēmpsia). PNEUMA's colloquial rendering loses the legal/theological register.
**Ruling:** "Does not call people based on reputation" adopted — a blend preserving the theological register while being understandable.

---

## Disagreement 7 — v.14: ἐκκλησία — "assembly" vs. "community"

| Agent | Rendering |
|-------|-----------|
| EMET | "assembly" |
| LOGOS | "assembly" |
| PNEUMA | "community gathers" |

**Issue:** ἐκκλησία is the Greek word for church/assembly. In this early context, it likely means the gathered worship assembly. "Assembly" preserves the term's specificity.
**Ruling:** "Assembly" retained. It is the precise liturgical term being used.
